title: Aesthetics Advertising: What Works for Practices (2026)
summary: Aesthetics advertising that fills books: what live Meta ads show, sample copy, offers that convert, Meta's health rules and how to measure cost per patient.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- Aesthetics advertising sells a subtle result from a provider the patient trusts. Put the injector on camera, name the treatment and make one clear first offer.
- The ads on the[aesthetics ad wall](https://www.sprites.ai/aesthetics-ads) show that most ads are short tests. The few that run for a year or more explain a named treatment or attach a concrete offer, and most of them are video.
- Best channels: Google Search for people ready to book, Instagram and Facebook for demand, Google Business Profile for trust, and email or text to past patients for rebooking.
- Measure cost per booked consult and cost per new patient, then compare both with what a patient spends in the first year.


## What live aesthetics ads show


The[aesthetics ad wall](https://www.sprites.ai/aesthetics-ads) lists live Meta ads from practices. The page shows the following.


Measure What the ads show


Advertisers 60


Ads 412


Share that is video About 45%


Median run time 15 days


Most common call to action Learn more, on about 28% of ads


A median run of 15 days tells you most ads are tested and replaced quickly. The ads that survive for months are the useful ones to study. Among the longest-running on the page, four of the six are video, and each one does a specific job.


- **It offers something free and useful.** One of the longest runners, at over 1,000 days, opens with "FREE Lip Filler Aftercare Download For Your Patients." It gives a resource first and asks for little.
- **It attaches a number to a named treatment.** A skin tightening ad that ran more than 600 days leads with a 50% discount and a free add-on, then says the offer is limited.
- **It explains the device.** An ad that ran over 460 days opens with "Emsculpt NEO is a non-invasive body contouring treatment that combines high-intensity focused electromagnetic (HIFEM) energy with…" The viewer learns what it is before being asked to book.
- **It borrows a familiar promise.** A facial ad that ran over a year leans on the idea that well-known people use it, and it is video.


The common thread is clarity. Each ad names one treatment or resource and gives the viewer a reason to act now or learn more. None of them is a general "visit our med spa" announcement.


## What an aesthetics ad actually sells


Aesthetics patients are not buying a procedure. They are buying a result that looks like themselves on a good day, from a person they trust with their face. That shapes every ad.


1. **The provider.** A 20 second video of the injector explaining what she does and what she will not do builds more trust than a polished clinic photo. People book a person, not a room.
2. **A natural result.** The fear is looking overdone. Show restrained work and say so in plain words, such as "conservative dosing, built up over visits."
3. **A low first step.** A first-treatment price, a consult credit or an intro membership lowers the risk of the first booking.
4. **A reason to come back.** Most revenue comes from repeat visits for neuromodulators, skin treatments and maintenance. An ad that points toward a membership or a series sets that up.


## Aesthetics advertising examples you can adapt


Replace the town, treatment and numbers with your own. Only claim what you can deliver.


### Provider video for Instagram and Facebook


**Video:** your lead injector, 20 to 30 seconds, speaking to camera in the treatment room. **Primary text:** "I'm Dana, a nurse injector in Plano. I focus on natural results, so people notice you look rested, not that you had something done. New patients can book a consult and a first treatment this month." **Headline:** "Meet your injector." **Button:** Book now.


### First-treatment offer


"New to us? Your first skin treatment is $149 (regular $225). Includes a skin consult with a licensed provider. Limited spots each month." State the price and the cap, and honor both.


### Device explainer


"Skin tightening without surgery. Here is how radiofrequency treatment works, how many sessions most people book and what the day after looks like. Watch, then book a consult if it fits." A plain explanation like this matches how the long-running device ads on the wall are built.


### Google Search ad


Responsive search ads allow up to 15 headlines of 30 characters. A set for an injectables practice:


Element Copy Characters


Headline 1 Botox and Filler in Plano 25


Headline 2 Licensed Nurse Injectors 24


Headline 3 Natural-Looking Results 23


Headline 4 New Patient Offer 17


Description 1 Book a consult with a licensed provider. See our 4.9-star reviews. 66


Description 2 Intro pricing for first-time patients. Online booking in two minutes. 68


## Which first offer works best


The offer is the part of an aesthetics ad you control most. Each type has a trade-off.


Offer What it does Watch for


First-treatment price Lowers the risk of the first visit Attracts bargain shoppers if the discount is too deep


Membership or intro plan Turns one visit into a recurring one Needs clear terms and an easy way to pause


Free or credited consult Works for higher-ticket devices and body contouring No-shows, so confirm by text


Free guide or aftercare download Collects emails and builds trust early Slower to turn into bookings, so follow up


Package or series price Raises order value for treatments that need several sessions Refund and expiry rules must be written down


Start with a first-treatment price for your most booked service and a consult offer for devices. Keep the discount at a level you can still make money on after the injector's time and product cost.


## Channels for aesthetics marketing


1. **Google Search.** Searchers typing "lip filler near me" or "Botox \[city\]" are close to booking. Bid on treatment plus town, and send each ad to a page about that treatment.
2. **Instagram and Facebook.** Best for creating demand, because people do not search until they have been nudged. Video and provider-led content do the heavy lifting. The[Facebook ads for med spas](https://www.sprites.ai/facebook-ads-for-med-spas) page goes deeper on structure.
3. **Google Business Profile.** Recent photos, review replies and a booking link. It costs nothing to keep current and influences who gets the call.
4. **Email and text to past patients.** Reminders when a neuromodulator treatment is due are often the cheapest bookings you will ever get.
5. **Referrals.** A simple "bring a friend" credit works because patients trust friends more than ads. For a broader view, see the[med spa marketing](https://www.sprites.ai/med-spa-marketing) guide.


## Meta rules for aesthetics ads


Meta's health and wellness rules mean an ad cannot assert or imply something personal about the viewer, such as a condition or their weight, before-and-after images are restricted, and unrealistic claims about results get rejected, so write about the treatment and the provider instead of the viewer's body.


## Creative checklist


- Put the provider on camera in the first three seconds.
- Name one treatment per ad.
- Say "natural" in specifics: conservative dosing, build over visits.
- State the first-visit price and any cap.
- Add captions to every video, since many people watch muted.
- Name the town and show a real room, not stock imagery.
- Refresh creative every few weeks, because the median run on the wall is only 15 days.


## How to measure aesthetics advertising


Clicks and likes do not pay for an injector's chair time. Track four numbers: leads, booked consults, patients who show and treat, and revenue in the first 12 months.


A worked example, with illustrative numbers. You spend $1,500 in a month and get 30 leads, which is $50 per lead. Forty percent book, so 12 consults, or $125 per booked consult. Six in ten of those show and treat, about 7 new patients, so your cost per new patient is about $214. If a new patient spends $600 in the first year and your gross margin is 60%, that is $360 of gross profit against $214 of ad cost. The channel clears the math. If the first-year spend were only $250, it would not.


Call every lead within five minutes where you can. In aesthetics, the practice that answers first often books the consult. ## FAQ


### What is aesthetics advertising?


It is paid and organic promotion for aesthetic practices, including injectables, skin treatments, devices and body contouring. The strongest ads feature the provider, name one treatment and make a clear first offer.


### What makes an aesthetics ad stand out?


A provider on camera, a natural-looking result and a specific offer. The longest-running ads on the[aesthetics ad wall](https://www.sprites.ai/aesthetics-ads) name a treatment or resource and give the viewer a reason to act, and most of them are video.


### Do video ads work better for aesthetics?


The ads on the wall suggest so. About 45% of them are video, and four of the six longest-running are video. Video lets patients meet the injector before they book, which is what the sale depends on.


### Are before and after photos allowed in Meta ads?


They are restricted under Meta's health and wellness rules, and ads that imply something about the viewer or promise unrealistic results can be rejected. Lead with the provider, the treatment and the offer, and check Meta's current policy before you run any result imagery.


### How much should an aesthetics practice spend on advertising?


Work backward from the value of a new patient. Find your cost per booked consult, apply your show and treatment rates, and compare cost per new patient with first-year gross profit. Increase spend only where that comparison holds.
